English: Mudbrick Hall
A simple, hastily constructed hall of sun-dried mudbricks, providing a basic space for the lords council and gathering of retainers.
Wooden Pavilion
A large timber structure, open to air and fit for small audiences, providing a more formal gathering place for retainers and minor nobles.
Open Court
An expansive, open-air court adorned with stone platforms for judgment, public displays, and the gathering of warriors and vassals.
Stone Audience Chamber
A sturdy audience chamber built of stone, offering security and dignity to gatherings, and impressing vassals with its permanence.
Pillar Hall
A grand hall supported by rows of carved stone pillars, with space for large gatherings, feasts, and the administration of justice.
Mandapa Hall
A lavish ceremonial hall with ornate mandapa-style porches, providing a prestigious center for royal ceremonies and feasts.
Royal Courtroom
A massive, secure chamber for the kings justice, lined with precious woods and murals, serving as the administrative heart of the realm.
Pillared Audience Hall
A monumental audience hall with towering pillars, gold inlay, and space for hundreds, signifying the rulers grandeur and administrative might.
Kings Durbar
A court of splendor, where the king holds audience with nobles and foreign envoys, its opulence matched only by the power it projects.
Imperial Durbar
The supreme seat of imperial authority, a palace of gold, marble, and colored stone, center of law, culture, and power for the entire realm.
